Ranger 7.name: Ranger 7
Ranger 7.info: Took 4,316 close-up photos in its last 17 minutes before hitting the Moon. America's first lunar success.
Ranger 7.story: My whole job lasted 17 minutes: take pictures, fall, and show Earth the Moon up close for the first time.
Ranger 7.photoCap: Ranger 7's first picture of the Moon, July 1964

Ranger 8 & Ranger 9.name: Ranger 8 & Ranger 9
Ranger 8 & Ranger 9.info: Photographed future Apollo landing areas. Ranger 9's final pictures were shown live on US television.
Ranger 8 & Ranger 9.story: Millions of people watched on TV as I raced toward the Moon, sending pictures until the very last second.
Ranger 8 & Ranger 9.photoCap: Ranger 7 at JPL in 1963; Rangers 8 and 9 were built the same way

Surveyor 1.name: Surveyor 1
Surveyor 1.info: First American soft landing on the Moon (2 Jun 1966). Sent back more than 11,000 photos and proved the ground could hold a spacecraft.
Surveyor 1.story: Everyone feared the Moon was deep dust that would swallow a lander. I touched down and proved it was solid.
Surveyor 1.photoCap: Surveyor 1's own shadow on the Moon, 1966

Lunar Orbiters 1–5.name: Lunar Orbiters 1–5
Lunar Orbiters 1–5.info: Mapped about 99% of the Moon to choose Apollo landing sites. Lunar Orbiter 1 took the first picture of Earth seen from near the Moon.
Lunar Orbiters 1–5.story: Five of us mapped the whole Moon so astronauts could pick a safe place to land — then we crashed so we wouldn't get in their way.
Lunar Orbiters 1–5.photoCap: Earth seen from near the Moon by Lunar Orbiter 1, 1966

Surveyor 3.name: Surveyor 3
Surveyor 3.info: Landed in April 1967. Apollo 12 astronauts walked to it in 1969 and brought its camera back to Earth. Claims that Earth germs survived inside were later doubted.
Surveyor 3.story: I waited two and a half years alone — then two astronauts walked over, said hello and took my camera home.
Surveyor 3.photoCap: Surveyor 3 in its crater, photographed by Apollo 12, 1969

Apollo 12 site — Intrepid.name: Apollo 12 site — Intrepid
Apollo 12 site — Intrepid.info: Landed within walking distance of Surveyor 3. Left the first full science station (ALSEP). The ascent stage was crashed later and the Moon ‘rang’ for about an hour.
Apollo 12 site — Intrepid.story: I landed so precisely that the astronauts could walk to an old robot lander parked nearby.
Apollo 12 site — Intrepid.model: NASA 3D model of a twin / related craft
Apollo 12 site — Intrepid.photoCap: Intrepid and Surveyor 3 together on the Moon, November 1969

Surveyor 5, 6 & 7.name: Surveyor 5, 6 & 7
Surveyor 5, 6 & 7.where: Sea of Tranquility · Sinus Medii · near Tycho
Surveyor 5, 6 & 7.info: Tested Moon soil chemistry. Surveyor 6 fired its engines and hopped about 2.5 m — the first liftoff from the Moon.
Surveyor 5, 6 & 7.story: I fired my engines, lifted off and landed a few steps away — the first rocket hop ever made on the Moon.
Surveyor 5, 6 & 7.photoCap: Moon panorama near Tycho crater taken by Surveyor 7, 1968

Apollo 11 site — Eagle.name: Apollo 11 site — Eagle
Apollo 11 site — Eagle.info: Eagle's descent stage, the flag (blown over at liftoff), a seismometer, a laser mirror, bootprints and about 100 other items left on 21 Jul 1969.
Apollo 11 site — Eagle.story: The astronauts flew home and I stayed behind with their bootprints, a flag and a mirror that scientists still hit with lasers.
Apollo 11 site — Eagle.photoCap: Buzz Aldrin beside Eagle's landing leg, July 1969

Apollo 13 S-IVB rocket stage.name: Apollo 13 S-IVB rocket stage
Apollo 13 S-IVB rocket stage.info: Apollo 13 never landed, but its third stage was aimed at the Moon. Apollo 12's seismometer felt the crash for over three hours.
Apollo 13 S-IVB rocket stage.story: My crew never reached the Moon, but I did — I hit it on purpose so a seismometer could listen to the Moon's insides.
Apollo 13 S-IVB rocket stage.model: NASA 3D model of a twin / related craft
Apollo 13 S-IVB rocket stage.photoCap: LRO view of an S-IVB crash crater (Apollo 16's stage; Apollo 13's made one like it)

Apollo 14 site — Antares.name: Apollo 14 site — Antares
Apollo 14 site — Antares.info: Left the Antares descent stage, a two-wheeled cart (MET), a laser mirror, a science station, and Alan Shepard's two golf balls.
Apollo 14 site — Antares.story: Alan Shepard hit two golf balls here. One is still lying in a crater — the only golf ball on the Moon.
Apollo 14 site — Antares.model: NASA 3D model of a twin / related craft
Apollo 14 site — Antares.photoCap: Edgar Mitchell with the two-wheeled cart, February 1971

Apollo 15 site — Falcon + Rover 1.name: Apollo 15 site — Falcon + Rover 1
Apollo 15 site — Falcon + Rover 1.info: First Lunar Roving Vehicle, the largest laser mirror (300 prisms), a science station, and the small Fallen Astronaut memorial. No NASA 3D model of the rover itself.
Apollo 15 site — Falcon + Rover 1.story: I'm the first car ever driven on another world. My battery is long dead, but I'm still parked where they left me.
Apollo 15 site — Falcon + Rover 1.model: NASA 3D model of a twin / related craft
Apollo 15 site — Falcon + Rover 1.photoCap: Jim Irwin with the first Lunar Roving Vehicle, July 1971

Apollo 16 site — Orion + Rover 2.name: Apollo 16 site — Orion + Rover 2
Apollo 16 site — Orion + Rover 2.info: Left the second rover, the first telescope used on the Moon (George Carruthers' ultraviolet camera), and Charlie Duke's family photo.
Apollo 16 site — Orion + Rover 2.story: An astronaut left a photo of his family in the dust. It's still here, faded by more than 50 years of sunlight.
Apollo 16 site — Orion + Rover 2.model: NASA 3D model of a twin / related craft
Apollo 16 site — Orion + Rover 2.photoCap: John Young jumps to salute the flag beside the lander and rover, April 1972

Apollo 17 site — Challenger + Rover 3.name: Apollo 17 site — Challenger + Rover 3
Apollo 17 site — Challenger + Rover 3.info: The last Apollo landing. The rover's fender was fixed with duct tape and maps; a plaque on the lander marks the end of the first human visits.
Apollo 17 site — Challenger + Rover 3.story: When my fender broke, the astronauts fixed it with duct tape and maps. Then the last humans left — and nobody has walked here since.
Apollo 17 site — Challenger + Rover 3.model: NASA 3D model of a twin / related craft

Lunar Prospector.name: Lunar Prospector
Lunar Prospector.where: Crater near the south pole, Moon
Lunar Prospector.info: Found signs of hydrogen at the poles, a clue to ice. It carried the ashes of geologist Eugene Shoemaker, the only person buried on the Moon.
Lunar Prospector.story: I carried a scientist who dreamed of the Moon all his life — now he rests there with me.

LCROSS + Centaur stage.name: LCROSS + Centaur stage
LCROSS + Centaur stage.info: The empty Centaur rocket hit a shadowed crater; LCROSS flew through the plume and found water before crashing too.
LCROSS + Centaur stage.story: We crashed into the darkest crater on the Moon, kicked up a cloud — and found water inside it.
LCROSS + Centaur stage.photoCap: LCROSS arrives in Florida for launch preparation, 2009

GRAIL — Ebb & Flow.name: GRAIL — Ebb & Flow
GRAIL — Ebb & Flow.info: Two spacecraft chased each other to map the Moon's gravity. Their crash site is named after astronaut Sally Ride.
GRAIL — Ebb & Flow.story: Two of us flew in a line, measuring the Moon's pull — and ended our mission together on a mountain named for Sally Ride.
GRAIL — Ebb & Flow.photoCap: Technicians lower the twin GRAIL spacecraft, 2011

LADEE.name: LADEE
LADEE.info: Studied the Moon's very thin atmosphere and floating dust, flying lower and lower until impact.
LADEE.story: I sniffed the Moon's thin air and floating dust, flying lower and lower until I touched the far side.

Odysseus (IM-1).name: Odysseus (IM-1)
Odysseus (IM-1).where: Near Malapert A, south pole, Moon
Odysseus (IM-1).info: First US landing on the Moon since 1972 (22 Feb 2024), built by Intuitive Machines for NASA's CLPS program. It landed on its side but still sent data.
Odysseus (IM-1).story: I landed on my side, but I still sent data home — the first American lander on the Moon in 52 years.
Odysseus (IM-1).photoCap: The Nova-C lander Odysseus before launch, 2024

Blue Ghost Mission 1.name: Blue Ghost Mission 1
Blue Ghost Mission 1.info: Firefly Aerospace's lander carried 10 NASA instruments (2 Mar 2025), worked for two weeks and photographed a lunar sunset.
Blue Ghost Mission 1.story: I watched the Earth cover the Sun from the Moon, then filmed a sunset before going to sleep.
Blue Ghost Mission 1.photoCap: Falcon 9 with Blue Ghost on the launch pad, January 2025

Athena (IM-2).name: Athena (IM-2)
Athena (IM-2).info: Carried NASA's PRIME-1 ice drill to the south pole (6 Mar 2025) but fell over in a crater and stopped after about a day.
Athena (IM-2).story: I came to drill for ice at the south pole but fell into a crater — the Moon is still a hard place to land.
Athena (IM-2).photoCap: Falcon 9 lifts off with the Athena lander, February 2025

Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter.name: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter
Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter.info: Maps the Moon in detail and has photographed every Apollo site, rover tracks and flag shadows from orbit.
Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter.story: I'm the Moon's photographer. From orbit I can still see the Apollo landers, rover tracks and even footpaths.
Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter.photoCap: LRO lowered into a space-simulation test chamber, 2008

Viking 1 Lander.name: Viking 1 Lander
Viking 1 Lander.info: First successful long-term Mars lander (20 Jul 1976). Tested soil for life and worked for over six years.
Viking 1 Lander.story: I took the first photo from the surface of Mars and tested its soil for signs of life.
Viking 1 Lander.photoCap: The first photo ever taken on Mars, with Viking 1's footpad, 1976

Viking 2 Lander.name: Viking 2 Lander
Viking 2 Lander.info: Twin of Viking 1, landed on the far side of the planet. Photographed thin frost on the ground in winter.
Viking 2 Lander.story: I saw frost on Mars — white ice on red rocks, far from home.
Viking 2 Lander.photoCap: Winter frost around the Viking 2 lander

Mars Pathfinder + Sojourner.name: Mars Pathfinder + Sojourner
Mars Pathfinder + Sojourner.info: Bounced down on airbags on 4 Jul 1997. Sojourner, the size of a microwave oven, was the first wheeled robot on another planet.
Mars Pathfinder + Sojourner.story: I'm the first rover on Mars — as small as a microwave oven. I never went more than a few metres from my lander.
Mars Pathfinder + Sojourner.photoCap: The Pathfinder landing site and the rock 'Yogi', 1997

Mars Polar Lander + Deep Space 2.name: Mars Polar Lander + Deep Space 2
Mars Polar Lander + Deep Space 2.info: Contact was lost during landing. Engineers think the engines shut off too early. The wreck has never been clearly found.
Mars Polar Lander + Deep Space 2.story: Nobody knows exactly where I am. My story taught engineers to test every tiny part twice.
Mars Polar Lander + Deep Space 2.photoCap: Mars Polar Lander during launch preparation, 1998

Spirit rover.name: Spirit rover
Spirit rover.info: Planned to work 90 days, lasted six years. Its stuck wheel scraped up bright soil that showed signs of ancient hot springs.
Spirit rover.story: I got stuck in sand — and my broken wheel dug up a clue that Mars once had hot springs.
Spirit rover.photoCap: Spirit's own camera looks across its deck after landing, January 2004

Opportunity rover.name: Opportunity rover
Opportunity rover.statusText: Silent since a dust storm in 2018
Opportunity rover.info: Built for 90 days, worked for almost 15 years and drove 45 km, farther than a marathon. Found rocks formed in water.
Opportunity rover.story: I was built for 90 days and kept going for almost 15 years — I drove more than a marathon on Mars.
Opportunity rover.photoCap: Opportunity's arm at work on a Martian rock

Phoenix lander.name: Phoenix lander
Phoenix lander.where: Vastitas Borealis, near the north pole, Mars
Phoenix lander.info: Dug into the ground and touched water ice. Winter ice later crushed a solar panel. It carries a DVD library called Visions of Mars.
Phoenix lander.story: I scraped the dirt and found real ice. I also carry a little DVD library for future Mars explorers to read.
Phoenix lander.photoCap: Phoenix sitting on Mars, photographed from orbit by MRO, 2008

Curiosity rover.name: Curiosity rover
Curiosity rover.info: A car-sized rover climbing Mount Sharp. Showed that Gale crater once held a lake that could have supported microbes.
Curiosity rover.story: I'm climbing a mountain in an old lake bed, reading Mars's history layer by layer like pages in a book.
Curiosity rover.photoCap: Curiosity's selfie at the 'Buckskin' drill site, 2015

InSight lander.name: InSight lander
InSight lander.info: Listened to the inside of Mars and recorded more than 1,300 marsquakes before dust covered its solar panels.
InSight lander.story: I put my ear to the ground and heard Mars rumble more than a thousand times.
InSight lander.photoCap: InSight's final selfie, covered in dust, 2022

Perseverance rover.name: Perseverance rover
Perseverance rover.info: Searching an old river delta for signs of past life and collecting rock samples for a future trip to Earth.
Perseverance rover.story: I'm collecting pieces of Mars in little tubes so that one day scientists on Earth can study them.

Ingenuity helicopter.name: Ingenuity helicopter
Ingenuity helicopter.info: First powered flight on another planet (19 Apr 2021). Planned for 5 flights, made 72. Carries a scrap of fabric from the Wright brothers' plane.
Ingenuity helicopter.story: They hoped I'd fly 5 times. I flew 72 — carrying a tiny piece of the Wright brothers' first airplane.
Ingenuity helicopter.photoCap: Ingenuity on Mars two years after its first flight, 2023

Three Forks sample depot.name: Three Forks sample depot
Three Forks sample depot.info: Perseverance laid 10 sealed tubes on the ground (2022–23) as a backup. The first sample depot on another planet.
Three Forks sample depot.story: We are ten little tubes of Mars rock, left on the ground on purpose and waiting for a ride to Earth.
Three Forks sample depot.photoCap: The last tube set down at the Three Forks depot, January 2023

Landing leftovers.name: Landing leftovers
Landing leftovers.where: Gale & Jezero craters and other sites, Mars
Landing leftovers.info: Every landing leaves parts behind: heat shields, backshells, parachutes and the sky cranes that lowered Curiosity (2012) and Perseverance (2021). Ingenuity photographed Perseverance's parachute in 2022.
Landing leftovers.story: We protected the rovers through a fiery fall, then dropped away. Now we lie in the dust like a trail of breadcrumbs.
Landing leftovers.model: NASA 3D print of the landing site
Landing leftovers.photoCap: Perseverance's backshell and parachute, photographed by Ingenuity, 2022

Mariner 9.name: Mariner 9
Mariner 9.info: First spacecraft to orbit another planet. Waited out a global dust storm, then mapped giant volcanoes and dry riverbeds. NASA expected its orbit to last until at least 2022.
Mariner 9.story: I arrived during a planet-wide dust storm, waited, and then saw the biggest volcano in the solar system appear.
Mariner 9.photoCap: Olympus Mons poking above the dust storm, seen by Mariner 9, 1971

Mars Global Surveyor.name: Mars Global Surveyor
Mars Global Surveyor.info: Mapped Mars for nine years and spotted gullies that look like they were carved by flowing water.
Mars Global Surveyor.story: For nine years I mapped every hill and valley of Mars, and found gullies that look like water made them.
Mars Global Surveyor.photoCap: Mars Global Surveyor prepared for launch, 1996

2001 Mars Odyssey.name: 2001 Mars Odyssey
2001 Mars Odyssey.statusText: Still working, nearly out of fuel
2001 Mars Odyssey.info: The longest-working spacecraft at Mars. Found ice under the surface and relays messages from rovers.
2001 Mars Odyssey.story: I've been at Mars longer than any other spacecraft, passing messages from rovers back to Earth.

Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.name: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter
Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.info: Its HiRISE camera can see objects the size of a kitchen table. It has photographed old landers, parachutes and crash sites.
Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.story: My camera is so sharp I can spot old landers and their parachutes lying on the ground.
Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.photoCap: MRO in the clean room before launch, 2005

MAVEN.name: MAVEN
MAVEN.statusText: Contact lost Dec 2025; mission ended Jun 2026
MAVEN.info: Studied how the Sun stripped away most of Mars's air. NASA lost contact on 6 Dec 2025 and ended the mission in June 2026.
MAVEN.story: I found out where Mars's air went — the Sun blew it away into space.

Voyager 1.name: Voyager 1
Voyager 1.info: The farthest human-made object. Took the ‘Pale Blue Dot’ photo of Earth. Expected to be one light-day from Earth around November 2026.
Voyager 1.story: Soon my messages will take a whole day to reach Earth. I'm the farthest thing humans have ever made.

Voyager 2.name: Voyager 2
Voyager 2.info: The only spacecraft to visit Uranus and Neptune. Entered interstellar space in 2018, about 21 billion km away. Carries a Golden Record.
Voyager 2.story: I'm the only visitor Uranus and Neptune have ever had, and I carry a golden record of Earth's music.

Pioneer 10.name: Pioneer 10
Pioneer 10.info: First to cross the asteroid belt and fly past Jupiter (1973). Carries a metal plaque about who sent it. (The plaque artwork shows unclothed people — our app uses its own drawing instead.)
Pioneer 10.story: I was the first to fly past Jupiter. Now I'm heading toward a red star and will need about 2 million years to get there.

Pioneer 11.name: Pioneer 11
Pioneer 11.info: Twin of Pioneer 10. First spacecraft to visit Saturn (1979). Uses the Pioneer 10 model.
Pioneer 11.story: I was the first visitor to Saturn's rings — now I drift toward the stars with a message from Earth.
Pioneer 11.model: NASA 3D model of a twin / related craft
Pioneer 11.photoCap: Pioneer 10 in 1972; Pioneer 11 was its identical twin

New Horizons.name: New Horizons
New Horizons.where: Kuiper Belt, leaving the solar system
New Horizons.info: First visit to Pluto (2015) and the farthest object ever explored, Arrokoth (2019). Carries some ashes of Pluto's discoverer, Clyde Tombaugh.
New Horizons.story: I showed the world Pluto's heart-shaped glacier, and I carry the man who discovered Pluto.
New Horizons.photoCap: New Horizons being prepared for launch, 2005

Vanguard 1.name: Vanguard 1
Vanguard 1.info: Tiny solar-powered satellite (1.5 kg), built by the US Navy; the Vanguard team later moved to NASA. The oldest human-made object still in orbit.
Vanguard 1.story: I'm the size of a grapefruit and I've circled Earth since 1958 — the oldest human-made thing still up there.
Vanguard 1.photoCap: Waiting for the Vanguard 1 launch, March 1958

MESSENGER.name: MESSENGER
MESSENGER.info: First spacecraft to orbit Mercury. Found water ice hiding in shadowed craters on the planet closest to the Sun.
MESSENGER.story: I found ice on Mercury, the planet closest to the Sun — hiding in craters where sunlight never reaches.

NEAR Shoemaker.name: NEAR Shoemaker
NEAR Shoemaker.info: First spacecraft to orbit an asteroid and the first to land on one, even though it was never built to land.
NEAR Shoemaker.story: I wasn't built to land, but I touched down gently on an asteroid anyway — and I'm still sitting on it.
NEAR Shoemaker.photoCap: NEAR Shoemaker during tests before launch, 1996

DART.name: DART
DART.info: Hit a small moon of an asteroid and shortened its orbit by 32 minutes — the first test of protecting Earth by pushing an asteroid.
DART.story: I crashed into an asteroid on purpose to prove humans can push one away if it ever heads for Earth.
DART.photoCap: DART launches on a Falcon 9, November 2021

Dawn.name: Dawn
Dawn.info: The only spacecraft to orbit two different worlds (Vesta and Ceres). Found bright salt deposits on Ceres. It will keep circling for decades.
Dawn.story: I visited two worlds in the asteroid belt and now I circle Ceres quietly, so I never touch it.
Dawn.photoCap: Dawn with its solar wings folded before launch, 2007

Deep Impact.name: Deep Impact
Deep Impact.where: Comet Tempel 1 · orbit around the Sun
Deep Impact.info: Fired an impactor into comet Tempel 1 on 4 July 2005 to see what was inside. The impactor's remains are part of the comet now.
Deep Impact.story: I threw a copper ball at a comet to see what was inside — like cracking open a cosmic egg.
Deep Impact.photoCap: The flash of Deep Impact's impactor hitting comet Tempel 1, July 2005

Ulysses.name: Ulysses
Ulysses.info: First spacecraft to fly over the Sun's north and south poles. Used Jupiter's gravity to swing out of the planets' plane.
Ulysses.story: Every other spacecraft looks at the Sun's middle. I flew over its top and its bottom.

Pioneer 4.name: Pioneer 4
Pioneer 4.info: First American spacecraft to escape Earth's gravity. Flew past the Moon at about 60,000 km.
Pioneer 4.story: I was the first American machine to break free of Earth — now I go round the Sun like a tiny planet.

Apollo 10 “Snoopy”.name: Apollo 10 “Snoopy”
Apollo 10 “Snoopy”.statusText: Lost in space; maybe found in 2019
Apollo 10 “Snoopy”.info: The dress-rehearsal lander flew within 15 km of the Moon, then was sent into orbit around the Sun. Astronomers think asteroid 2018 AP4 may be Snoopy.
Apollo 10 “Snoopy”.story: I practised the Moon landing without touching down, then drifted off around the Sun. Astronomers think they may have spotted me again.
Apollo 10 “Snoopy”.model: NASA 3D model of a twin / related craft
Apollo 10 “Snoopy”.photoCap: Snoopy's ascent stage photographed from Apollo 10, May 1969

Apollo 12 S-IVB rocket stage.name: Apollo 12 S-IVB rocket stage
Apollo 12 S-IVB rocket stage.info: In 2002 an amateur astronomer found a ‘new asteroid’ (J002E3). It turned out to be Apollo 12's third stage, painted white.
Apollo 12 S-IVB rocket stage.story: In 2002 someone discovered a new asteroid near Earth. Surprise — it was me, a leftover Apollo rocket stage.
Apollo 12 S-IVB rocket stage.model: NASA 3D model of a twin / related craft
Apollo 12 S-IVB rocket stage.photoCap: A Saturn V third stage drifting away (Apollo 8's, same type as Apollo 12's)

Spitzer Space Telescope.name: Spitzer Space Telescope
Spitzer Space Telescope.info: Saw the universe in heat (infrared) and helped find seven Earth-sized planets around the star TRAPPIST-1.
Spitzer Space Telescope.story: I saw the universe in heat instead of light — and helped find seven Earth-sized planets around one star.

Kepler Space Telescope.name: Kepler Space Telescope
Kepler Space Telescope.info: Watched stars for tiny dips in brightness and found more than 2,600 planets, showing that planets are common.
Kepler Space Telescope.story: I stared at stars and waited for them to blink — and found thousands of new worlds.

MarCO-A & MarCO-B.name: MarCO-A & MarCO-B
MarCO-A & MarCO-B.info: Briefcase-sized satellites that followed InSight to Mars and relayed its landing news live. First CubeSats in deep space. Generic CubeSat model only.
MarCO-A & MarCO-B.story: We're as small as a briefcase, but we flew to Mars and told Earth that InSight had landed safely.
MarCO-A & MarCO-B.model: NASA 3D model of a twin / related craft
MarCO-A & MarCO-B.photoCap: An engineer with both MarCO CubeSats, 2018

Deep Space 1.name: Deep Space 1
Deep Space 1.info: Tested an ion engine with a gentle blue glow, plus self-driving navigation. Flew past a comet.
Deep Space 1.story: My engine pushes as softly as a sheet of paper on your hand — but it never stops pushing.

Stardust.name: Stardust
Stardust.info: Caught comet dust in a super-light foam called aerogel and sent it to Earth in a capsule (2006). The spacecraft stayed in space.
Stardust.story: I caught comet dust in a foam lighter than air and sent it home in a capsule — then I stayed behind.
Stardust.photoCap: Stardust's comet-dust capsule after landing in Utah, 2006
